asset_title: How Much Recruiters Actually Make Per Hire: Commission Rates by Recruiter Type in 2026
distinct_angle: Breaks down what 'per hire' pay really means across agency/contingency, retained, RPO, and in-house recruiters, with real commission percentages and dollar ranges by role and seniority from public salary and industry-fee data, answering the recruiter's-own-earnings question the keyword actually asks instead of restating employer cost-per-hire.

How much do recruiters get paid per recruit?
What type of recruiters make the most money?

Defines recruiter pay as split between steady corporate salaries and volatile agency commissions ($60k-$110k average total comp), then breaks down: Corporate/In-House ($100k-$162k, base+bonus) → Agency/Third-Party ($50k-$90k standard billers, $150k-$250k+ top performers, commission-based) → Executive Search ($110k-$300k+, highest commissions) → a compensation-model table (Salary+Bonus vs Base+Commission vs Pure Commission, with structure/earnings potential/pros-cons) → agency fee mechanics (15%-25% of first-year salary) → top-paying industries (IT/Tech $94,315, Financial Services $88,799, Legal $84,725, Pharma/Biotech $84,063).
